# Owner wash 01: what the simulation predicts

> **Publication note (12 October 2026).** When this repository was published, the commit and
> branch identifiers of the private development history were removed from this file and from the
> two wash records of this wash, and in those two records the owner's name was replaced by "the

**Written before the owner's result was known. Do not edit this file afterwards.** The result and
its comparison with this prediction go in a separate file. Finished on 10 October 2026 at 22:50 BST;
the owner looks at the plates on the morning of the 11th.

The wash: four plates with raw egg yolk, Eco 50, one Finish Powerball Ultimate capsule, in the
owner's Bosch SMV4HAX40G. The plan is `owner-wash-01-egg-yolk.md`; what he set up is in
`docs/reference/calibration_runs/2026-10-10_egg_plates/`. His README first said the oven pair had
"20 hours" at 80 C; it was corrected to 2 hours, which he confirmed. The headline
below is therefore the 2-hour reading. The 20-minute reading is given beside it.

## 1. The prediction in plain words

With 3 g of yolk on each plate, the model says the two plates facing the middle come out clean:
the air-dried one (9123) spotless, the oven-dried one (9122) clean with one or two specks at most.
The oven-dried plate turned to the left wall (9121) sits on the edge of clean: a dozen specks near
the edge of the well when the rest of the load is in the machine, clean when the plates are alone.
The small plate (9124) comes out with about fifty specks in a ring near the edge of its well, but
only because 3 g on its small well is twice as thick as on the others; with a film as thin as on
the large plates it comes out spotless. More than 99.8 % of the yolk is removed from every plate in
every case. The model is sure of the order (9123 cleanest, then 9122, then 9121) and of little
else: the verdicts do not move with the simulation seed or the visibility band, but each of the
five most influential parameters, moved to the ends of its registered range, turns all four plates
clean or all four dirty, and so does halving or doubling the amount of yolk.

How much the answer depends on the oven time: only plate 9121 changes verdict (dirty at 2 hours,
clean at 20 minutes, case b), and plate 9122 goes from two specks to none. In the model 2 hours at
80 C gives a bake index of 0.195 and 20 minutes gives 0.037, which slows the reaction by about 16 %
and 3 %. Whether the air pair was dry or still wet changes nothing on 9123 and about a fifth of
the residue on 9124.

## 3. How the wash was built

- Programme `eco_50`, no options; official tier (2 mm blocks); level seed 20261010; simulation
  seeds 1, 2, 3; the game's default set with the capsule's composition in it; dose 12.9 g; the
  dispenser free and both arms turning (the session's checks).
- Plates. The three large ones are `dinner_plate_porcelain_270` (27 cm, 30 mm deep), the catalogue
  kind closest to his 27 cm wide-rimmed plate and the one the loader already uses for it. The small
  one is `dessert_plate_porcelain_190`: the catalogue has no plain plate between 19 and 23 cm, and
  the 22 cm pieces in it are deep plates. His plates are earthenware with a wider rim; their
  profiles are not measured.
- Soil. `egg_yolk_dried` (raw yolk, spread, solids 0.5) on 0.67 of the well, 3 g wet, about 1.5 g
  dry (the wash lays down 1.47 to 1.56 g per plate: the set has a 5 % scatter of the amount). Mean
  dry loading 7.3 mg/cm2 on the large plates and 15 mg/cm2 on the small one. Oven pair: heat
  history `warm` (80 C for 2 h; for the other reading `soil.heatDuration[warm]` = 1200 s), then a
  quarter of an hour at room conditions. Air pair: no heat, 2.25 h (0.58 h for the 20-minute
  reading; 0.1 h for "still wet"). In the model a film this thick is not dry after 2 hours on the
  counter anyway, which agrees with the gloss in his photographs.
- Slots. Rear rows, from his photographs: 9121 at the far left, 9122 in the seventh gap from the
  left (`slot_06`), 9123 in the eighteenth (`slot_17`), 9124 near the right end. 9122 and 9123
  were let go at the pose `list_slots` suggests and settled. 27 cm plates cannot stand in the ten
  gaps between them: the cutlery basket at the front centre is in the way, as in his photograph.
- The turned plates. `list_slots` has no pose for a plate turned round, so every clear pose near
  the slot with the face to the wall was let go in the session's physics, and the one kept was the
  one that came to rest held by the rear rows, nearest the wall, with the basket still sliding in.
  Both turned plates rest leaning outwards on the side of the basket (33 and 20 degrees), as his
  outer plates do in IMG_9125 and IMG_9126.
- Interpenetration. No true-shape overlap in either load (deepest 0.00 mm in case a, 0.17 mm in
  case b). The collision shapes touch by 0.26 mm (a) and 0.64 mm (b, plate 9121 against a basket
  wire; the loader's limit is 0.5 mm). Plate 9121 overhangs the basket's plan by 9.5 mm, as his
  does, and in case b the loader lists it as not at rest: it crept 10 mm while the other pieces
  were placed.
- Case b, stand-ins for the load of IMG_9126, placed only where they moved no yolk plate: two
  `dinner_plate_porcelain_270` with tomato sauce in the right side rows; one
  `pasta_bowl_porcelain_230` (pasta starch) at the front left; one `cereal_bowl_porcelain_160`
  (porridge) at the front right; four forks, three knives, four dessert spoons, two teaspoons in
  the cutlery basket; in the upper basket two `wine_glass_generic_200` and a `mixing_bowl_pp_3l`
  standing in for his plastic colander. Left out because they found no seat: the second deep bowl,
  a third glass, and the catalogue's steel colander (it blocks the upper basket or the tablet's
  path wherever it is put). The stand-ins carry 5.2 g of dry soil; their own verdicts are not
  predictions.

## 4. What the model says the programme did

| | |
|---|---|
| Duration | 17 689 s, 4 h 54 min 49 s (printed 4:55) |
| Water | 9.5 L in all; the main wash runs on 4.0 L |
| Energy | 0.90 kWh (printed 0.836) |
| Pre-rinse | cold, about 23 C; the capsule is released between 15 and 20 min |
| Main wash | capsule dissolved by 25 min (3.2 g/L); 33 C at 20 min, 45 C at 25 min, highest 5-minute sample 48.7 C at 30 min; then no heating: 48.0 C at 1 h 05, 47.0 C at 2 h, 46.4 C at 2 h 40, 42 C when it drains at about 2 h 57 |
| pH in the main wash | 10.56 falling to 10.37, then 10.4 to 10.5 |
| Protease in the liquor | 73 mg/L at 20 min, 95 at 25 min, 93 at 30 min, 86 at 50 min, 82 at 1 h 05, 77 at 1 h 30, 72 at 2 h, 68 at 2 h 30, 66 at 2 h 55; 7 and then 2 mg/L carried into the rinses |
| Final rinse | heated to about 60 C at 3 h 20 min; drying to the end |
| Spraying | 3 h 16 min in all: lower arm 28 to 31 L/min, upper arm and roof 26 to 28 L/min, alternating |
| Wells of the four plates | wet all the time the spray runs; jets strike 0.04 to 1.5 % of the time; liquor exchange on the turned plates 0.88 and 1.03 against 1.16 and 1.20 on those facing the middle |

In this wash the model removes about 17 to 22 mg/cm2 of dry oven-dried yolk and about 25 to 30
mg/cm2 of air-dried yolk before the main wash ends (read from the 6 g replay). The mean on the
large plates is 7.3 mg/cm2, so what is left at 3 g is the thickest few places of a film the model
takes to vary by 30 % from patch to patch.

## 5. What would contradict the model, and what each would mean

1. **9122 (oven-dried, facing the middle) with a film or patches over a visible part of the well.**
   The model is too optimistic at 50 C with this capsule: the reaction rate, the protease level
   or its survival is too high, or the oven penalty too small. If 9123 is clean at the same time,
   it is the oven penalty (the model slows 2-hour yolk by only 16 %).
2. **9123 (air-dried, facing the middle) not clean.** This is the firmest prediction. Ageing cannot
   explain it, so the kinetics or the enzyme level are too high, or the long main wash sprays less
   than modelled (the manual hints at intermittent spraying).
3. **Residue only as lines along the thickest fork ridges, on any plate.** The kinetics may be
   right; the model's even film is wrong for a fork-spread soil. Ridges thicker than about 0.35 mm
   wet exceed what the model says this wash removes. The record then needs the ridges described,
   and `soil.applicationCv[spread]` is the parameter this informs.
4. **9121 much dirtier than 9122 (a film over a large part of the well, not a dozen specks).**
   Facing matters more than modelled: a face turned to the wall and leaning over gets much less
   fresh liquor than the 25 % less the model gives it (`soil.supplyExchange`, and the water side).
5. **9121 as spotless as 9122.** No contradiction: the model has it clean in three of the four cases of section 2 (alone or with the load, 2 hours or 20 minutes).
   It would say the load around the plates costs less than modelled.
6. **9124 spotless although it carried as much yolk as a large plate (a visibly thicker film).**
   The model removes too little per area, the opposite error to 1 and 2.
7. **9124 dirty although its film was as thin as on the others.** A turned face cleans worse than
   modelled (as 4), or a small plate at the end of the row is reached worse than modelled.
8. **A uniform matt film over the whole soiled area of any plate.** The model predicts specks at
   the thickest places, never an even film. An even film means removal stopped everywhere at once:
   the enzyme died or the soak stopped spraying.
9. **All four dirty.** As the plan says: too optimistic on Eco with this capsule. The first
   suspects are the five parameters of section 2, in that order of reach.
10. **All four spotless.** Agrees on 9122 and 9123. The specks predicted on 9121 and 9124 are then
    not there, which the amount of yolk alone could explain.

## 6. What this wash cannot tell

- Which of rate, enzyme level and enzyme survival is wrong. They trade against each other, and
  end states only bound a rate.
- Whether facing matters, cleanly. The turned plates also stand at the ends of the row and lean 20
  to 33 degrees where their partners stand upright, and the air-dried turned plate is the small
  one with an unknown amount on it.
- Anything that turns on the amount. It was not weighed, the film is in ridges and bare stripes,
  and the model's verdicts flip between 1.5 g and 6 g.
- What the programme did. There is no temperature or power log; the course above is the model's
  assumption. The clock times of start and finish would at least fix the duration.
- How his plates stand. The catalogue plates are not his: the model's middle plates tip 2 to 4
  degrees towards their faces where his lean about 3 degrees outwards, and the rest of the load is
  made of stand-ins with assumed soils.
- Repeatability. It is one wash, judged by eye.
